Let $X_1, \dots, X_n$ be an i.i.d. sample from an Exponential($\theta$) distribution. A $100(1-\alpha)\%$ confidence interval for the parameter $\theta$ is given by:

A. $ \left[ \frac{\chi^2_{1-\alpha/2}(2n)}{2n\bar{X}}, \frac{\chi^2_{\alpha/2}(2n)}{2n\bar{X}} \right] $

B. $ \left[ \frac{\chi^2_{\alpha/2}(2n)}{2n\bar{X}}, \frac{\chi^2_{1-\alpha/2}(2n)}{2n\bar{X}} \right] $

C. $ \left[ \frac{2n\bar{X}}{\chi^2_{\alpha/2}(2n)}, \frac{2n\bar{X}}{\chi^2_{1-\alpha/2}(2n)} \right] $

D. $ \left[ \frac{\chi^2_{1-\alpha/2}(n)}{2n\bar{X}}, \frac{\chi^2_{\alpha/2}(n)}{2n\bar{X}} \right] $

(Note: $\chi^2_p(k)$ denotes the upper $p$-th quantile of the chi-squared distribution with $k$ degrees of freedom.)

ground_truth.answer: A

1.3 Let the joint distribution of $Y_1$ and $Y_2$ be $\text{MVN}(\boldsymbol{\mu}, \mathbf{V})$ with

$\boldsymbol{\mu} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{V} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 9 \end{pmatrix}$.

(a) Obtain an expression for $\mathbf{y}^T\mathbf{V}^{-1}\mathbf{y}$. What is its distribution?
records.final_answer:
The inverse of the covariance matrix is  

\[
\mathbf V^{-1}= \frac1{35}\begin{pmatrix}9 & -1\\[2pt]-1 & 4\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Hence, for \(\mathbf y=(y_1,y_2)^{\!T}\),

\[
\mathbf y^{\!T}\mathbf V^{-1}\mathbf y
   =\frac1{35}\Bigl(9y_1^{2}-2y_1y_2+4y_2^{2}\Bigr).
\]

If \(\mathbf Y\sim\text{MVN}(\boldsymbol\mu,\mathbf V)\) and we set \(\mathbf y=\mathbf Y-\boldsymbol\mu\), then  

\[
(\mathbf Y-\boldsymbol\mu)^{\!T}\mathbf V^{-1}(\mathbf Y-\boldsymbol\mu)
   \sim \chi^{2}_{\,2},
\]

a chi‑square distribution with 2 degrees of freedom.
